nodes.name: Hydrothermal Carbonization
nodes.procedure: Typically, sucrose (10 g) was dissolved in distilled water (80 mL) by stirring the mixture charged to a Teflon-lined autoclave (100 mL). The autoclave was then sealed, and transferred to an electric oven maintained at 190 °C for 2 h. Afterwards, the black products obtained were rinsed with distilled (DI) water and ethanol repeatedly, then dried overnight at 80 °C.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of necklace-like carbon. Typically, sucrose (10 g) was dissolved in distilled water (80 mL) ... dried overnight at 80 °C.

nodes.name: Metal Ion Adsorption Hydrothermal
nodes.procedure: Necklace-like carbon (0.5 g) were dispersed in Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (10 M, 60 mL) and Co(NO3)2·6H2O aqueous solution (10 M, 60 mL) by agitation with a magnetic stirrer for 2 h followed by ultrasonication for 0.5 h. The obtained mixture was then charged to a Teflon-lined autoclave, sealed and heated to 180 °C for 10 h to ensure Ni and Co ions adsorbed on the surface of necklace-like carbon sufficiently. Then, the Ni-Co-CI precursor was obtained by centrifuge.

nodes.name: Calcination for NCO variants
nodes.procedure: The as-prepared precursor was subsequently subject to calcination at 450 °C for 1 h, with the ramp rate set to 2 °C min⁻¹ in air to develop the necklace-like triple shelled, concentric hollow structures. To investigate the effect of temperature, the temperature was varied from 310, 340, to 370 °C with other conditions remaining constant, and the obtained samples are denoted as NCO-310, NCO-340, and NCO-370, respectively.

nodes.name: Chemical Reduction
nodes.procedure: The reduced TMO were synthesized by soaking the pristine powder in 1 M NaBH4 aqueous solution for 2 h, then collected by centrifugation, rinsed with DI water then subsequently kept for 12 h in a vacuum oven maintained at 80 °C to dry.
